Answer_with_writing_sample: Choosing between "lorsque" and "quand" in French can be a bit tricky for beginners, but it’s not as daunting as it seems! You can use it in questions, like "Quand est-ce que tu viens?" (When are you coming?), or in statements, such as "Je vais au cinéma quand j'ai le temps" (I go to the movies when I have time). On the other hand, "lorsque" is a bit more formal and is typically used in written French or more serious conversations. It often implies a specific moment in time, like in the sentence "Lorsque je suis arrivé, il pleuvait" (When I arrived, it was raining). So, if you’re chatting with friends or in a casual setting, "quand" is your go-to. But if you’re writing an essay or speaking in a formal context, "lorsque" can add a nice touch of sophistication.
